label: Turkey Breast (raw)
note: Whole-muscle raw breast (bone-in, boneless roast, tenderloin, cutlet). Deli/lunchmeat names are owned by turkey-lunchmeat (index 141, earlier = wins) and ground by ground-turkey (index 3); the excludes here are belt-and-braces so a name those two miss can never land as a raw-breast price. 'smoked'/'cooked' fenced (heat-and-eat is a different price class). RELAX \bfrozen\b - most whole turkey breasts ship frozen and the global token would otherwise blank the row.

label: Dried Arbol Chiles
note: 'rbol\b' (not '\barbol\b') so both 'Chile de Arbol' and the accented 'Chile de Arbol' spelling match without putting a non-ASCII byte in the rules file. Nothing else in a grocery catalog ends in 'rbol'. Ground/powder forms fall to chili-powder (index 317, earlier); the powder exclude makes that a rule instead of a position.

label: Dried Guajillo Chiles
note: Unique word. Same powder/paste fencing as arbol.

label: Dried Ancho Chiles
note: '\bancho\b' cannot match 'anchovy' (word char follows), but anchovy/anchovies are excluded anyway because that is exactly the class of near-miss that ships a fish price as a chile price. 'Ancho Chile Powder' is claimed by chili-powder first AND excluded here.

label: Diced / Cubed Ham
note: Reciprocal exclude added to deli-ham (index 33: bare '\bham\b' was claiming 'Great Value Diced Ham'). RELAX \bwater\b - 'Water Added' is on nearly every ham label and the global water token (bottled water) was blanking real diced-ham rows.

label: Sazon Seasoning
note: 'saz.n' covers 'sazon' and the accented 'sazon' without non-ASCII bytes. Reciprocal exclude added to achiote-paste (index 389), which was claiming 'Sazon Goya con Culantro y Achiote' through its annatto/achiote include. Adobo deliberately NOT folded in: an 8 oz adobo shaker and a 1.41 oz sazon box are different price classes and folding them would corrupt the per-oz.

label: Eggplant (each)
note: Globe eggplant sold by each. Specialty varieties and organic are excluded on the variety-pricing precedent (the red-onion rule) so a $3 Japanese eggplant can never set the price of a $1.48 globe. The eggs commodity's '\beggs?\b' cannot reach 'eggplant' (word boundary fails), verified in the probe.

label: Brown Gravy Mix (dry packet)
note: RELAX '\bmix\b(?!\s*(?:&|and)\s*match)' (verbatim GLOBAL_EXCLUDE string) - without it every 'gravy mix' product name is globally dropped and the row is born permanently empty. jarred-gravy (index 354) already excludes mix/packet/envelope/dry/powder/granules, so the ready-to-serve jars stay put and the packets fall through to here: fenced in BOTH directions.

label: Chicken Livers
note: Meat-case tubs. Pet treats are the live hazard here (freeze-dried chicken liver dog treats are per-oz expensive and would blow up the row) so pet tokens are excluded at the rule layer as well as by the category-exclude library.

label: Sweet Soy Sauce (Kecap Manis)
note: RELAX \bsauce\b. Reciprocal exclude added to soy-sauce (index 325, which relaxes sauce and was claiming both 'ABC Sweet Soy Sauce Kecap Manis' and 'Kecap Manis'): soy-sauce += 'sweet\s+soy', 'ke[ct]jap|kecap'. Fenced both ways - a plain Kikkoman still lands in soy-sauce (probe verified).

label: Caraway Seeds
note: Spice jar only; caraway is a NAMED INGREDIENT of rye bread, kraut and havarti, so those carriers are fenced (the blueberries-as-Bai-beverage class, applied preventively).

label: Poultry Seasoning
note: Phrase-anchored ('seasoning' is not a GLOBAL_EXCLUDE token - only 'seasoned' is, and it does not substring-match). Rubs/brines are a different product and price class.

label: Wild Rice
note: 100% wild rice only. The mapper's note allowed 'wild-rice-forward blends'; I tightened that to a hard blend exclude because a long-grain-and-wild box is mostly white rice at a fraction of the per-oz and would ALWAYS win the cheapest slot, publishing a wild-rice price that is not wild rice. rice (index 56) already excludes 'wild', so it is fenced both ways with no edit needed there (probe verified: 'Great Value Wild Rice' resolved to nobody, not to rice).

label: Doubanjiang (Chili Bean Paste)
note: RELAX \bsauce\b (the LKK jar is literally named 'Chili Bean Sauce'). Reciprocal exclude added to chili-beans (index 333) for 'chili\s+bean\s+sauce'/'toban': today the global sauce token already blocks chili-beans from those jars, but that protection would evaporate the day anyone gives chili-beans a sauce relax, so the fence is written explicitly.

label: Fennel Seed / Ground Fennel
note: Whole seed accepted as the same commodity (grinding at home is not a price flip - the mapper's call, and both forms sit in the same jar/price class). Bare 'fennel' deliberately NOT an include so fresh per-lb fennel bulb cannot land in an oz row.

label: Snow / Sugar Snap Peas (fresh)
note: Fresh edible-podded peas. frozen-peas (index 248) owns shelled green peas and relaxes \bfrozen\b; this row does NOT relax it, so a frozen snap-pea bag is dropped rather than mixed into a fresh per-oz. Reciprocal exclude added to sugar (index ~), which was claiming 'Sugar Snap Peas' through its bare '\bsugar\b' include - a pre-existing latent hijack the probe surfaced.

label: Horseradish Sauce (creamy)
note: RELAX \bsauce\b. No reciprocal edit needed on horseradish (index 367): it has no sauce relax, so every '...Horseradish Sauce' name is globally blocked there and falls through to here - verified in the probe. Its live cells ('Inglehoffer Creamy Style PREPARED Horseradish', 'Thick-n-Creamy Horseradish') are prepared root and are protected here by the prepared/root excludes, so the existing row cannot be stolen.

label: Corned Beef Brisket (raw)
note: SEASONAL: shelf presence peaks around March, so this row is expected to sit EMPTY most of the year. It is registered with empty cells rather than being fed a canned corned-beef-hash price. Reciprocal exclude added to frozen-corn, whose include 'cut\s+(?:golden\s+)?corn' (no trailing boundary) was matching 'Flat CUT CORNed Beef Brisket' - a genuine cross-aisle hijack the probe caught.

label: Pigeon Peas / Gandules (canned)
note: RELAX \bcanned\b - the mapper's decision note claimed 'canned' is not a GLOBAL_EXCLUDE token; it IS one ('\bcanned\b'), so without the relax any 'Canned Green Pigeon Peas' name is dropped. Dried gandules excluded (a dry bean per-oz against a canned-with-liquid per-oz is a false cheapest). frozen-peas' 'green\s+peas\b' cannot reach 'Green Pigeon Peas' (probe verified).

label: Aji Amarillo Paste
note: 'aj.\s+amarillo' matches both 'aji' and the accented 'aji' spellings with no non-ASCII byte. Bare 'amarillo' is deliberately NOT an include: 'Arroz Amarillo' (yellow rice) would hijack the row - and arroz/rice are excluded for the same reason. No sauce relax: the commodity is the jarred paste.

label: Rye Bread (loaf)
note: Reciprocal exclude added to bread (index 25): its bare '\bbread\b' was claiming 'Pepperidge Farm Jewish Rye Bread' and 'Marble Rye Bread Loaf'. Rye runs 2-3x a white sandwich loaf, so the variety-pricing precedent bars the fold in both directions. Checked against the live bread cells (all white/wheat sandwich loaves) - the reciprocal exclude drops none of them.
